tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Begin with the README to understand the service's purpose, supported workflows, and operational model. The onboarding guide then turns that broad map into a contributor-oriented explanation of the architecture, domain vocabulary, and development conventions used throughout the remaining steps.

tour.title: Boot and Build
tour.description: With the product map established, follow the Spring Boot entry point to see how the application starts. The Maven descriptor defines the Java 25, Spring, Neo4j, AI, parsing, and observability toolchain, while the default properties file shows the configuration surface that shapes runtime behavior.
tour.languageLesson: Spring Boot uses an annotated Java application class as the composition root, while Maven's POM declares the reproducible dependency and build model around it. Profile-specific properties can override the shared defaults without changing code.

tour.title: REST API Boundary
tour.description: The controllers expose the main schema, document, and query workflows introduced in the README and delegate validated requests into application services. The global exception handler completes this boundary by translating domain failures into consistent API errors, keeping transport concerns outside the core workflows.

tour.title: Persistent Domain Model
tour.description: Behind the API, these Neo4j-backed entities define the durable vocabulary shared by every workflow: knowledge bases, schemas, uploaded documents, chunks, and AI profiles. Their high fan-in makes them the best foundation for understanding how later services coordinate state without collapsing domain rules into controllers or repositories.

tour.title: Schema Foundation
tour.description: The schema document defines the graph contract that constrains extraction and querying, while the registry service enforces lifecycle and persistence rules around that contract. The two bootstrap JSON schemas make the abstraction concrete by showing how maintenance and legal-contract domains declare labels, properties, keys, and relationships.
tour.languageLesson: JSON schema resources act as declarative domain models: code can validate and interpret them while the domain-specific labels and relationships remain data rather than hard-coded Java branches.

tour.title: Schema Draft Lifecycle
tour.description: Building on the stable schema contract, this workflow discovers candidate structures, analyzes evidence, evaluates readiness, and publishes an approved revision. The draft controller exposes that lifecycle, while the focused services make each transition explicit and durable instead of treating model output as immediately trustworthy.

tour.title: Document Processing Pipeline
tour.description: Once a knowledge base has a usable schema, document processing advances content through explicit parsing, chunk preparation, embedding persistence, and graph-extraction stages. The orchestration service owns workflow invariants across those boundaries, making partial progress and failures easier to reason about than a single monolithic ingestion method.

tour.title: Constrained Graph Extraction
tour.description: The extraction subsystem turns prepared chunks into graph candidates through a model adapter, then validates those candidates against the active schema before writing them. This is the central safety boundary for model-produced structure: transformation, validation, and persistence remain separate so invalid labels, relationships, or properties cannot silently enter Neo4j.

tour.title: AI Runtime Control
tour.description: The AI profile service and runtime model factory resolve provider and model choices at knowledge-base scope, while runtime settings govern the mutable operational knobs used by processing and querying. The OpenAI and LM Studio profiles demonstrate how the same application workflows can target hosted or local OpenAI-compatible providers without leaking provider selection into feature services.

tour.title: Query Safety Pipeline
tour.description: After ingestion has produced a schema-constrained graph, the query path combines hybrid retrieval with natural-language answer orchestration and generated Cypher. Generation, validation, and execution are deliberately separate stages so schema checks, read-only policy, limits, and database execution remain deterministic even when a model proposes the query.

tour.title: Persistence Adapters
tour.description: The repositories map the durable domain model from Step 4 onto Neo4j lookups and relationships, while the binary-storage abstraction keeps uploaded content outside the graph. Its local-filesystem implementation and reconciliation-oriented service boundary show how the application separates graph metadata from binary lifecycle concerns.

tour.title: Safe Observability
tour.description: Cross-cutting observability records AI workflow spans and metrics while preserving the privacy boundary around prompts, documents, model responses, and generated graph content. Metadata-safe logging helpers support ordinary diagnostics, and the Langfuse profile shows how controlled trace export is enabled independently from normal application logs.

tour.title: Local Infrastructure
tour.description: The Compose topology supplies Neo4j for graph persistence and an optional local Langfuse stack for the observability path from Step 12. Reading it near the end connects the application's adapter boundaries to the databases, telemetry services, health checks, and persistent volumes required for a realistic local environment.
tour.languageLesson: Docker Compose uses service dependencies, health checks, networks, and named volumes to coordinate a multi-container development environment while keeping stateful data persistent across container recreation.

tour.title: End-to-End Verification
tour.description: Finish with the canonical full-flow integration test, which exercises the architecture as a connected system rather than isolated classes. The architecture-boundary test guards the layering learned across the tour, while Testcontainers configuration supplies an actual Neo4j instance for deterministic persistence coverage.
